network.tdh.explainer.title: TDH
network.tdh.explainer.metadataDescriptio: What TDH is, how to read your own, and how it is calculated, specified, proved and checked against 6529.io every day.
network.tdh.explainer.intro: Every eligible card you hold earns its whole days held, weighted by rarity and multiplied by a boost for collecting sets. It counts toward your Level, and is checked in public every day.
network.tdh.explainer.eligible: Meme Lab cards and received xTDH do not count.
network.tdh.explainer.minute.title: TDH in a minute
network.tdh.explainer.minute.hold.title: Hold.
network.tdh.explainer.minute.hold.body: Each copy counts the whole days since you got it. Selling it removes its days.
network.tdh.explainer.minute.weigh.title: Weigh.
network.tdh.explainer.minute.weigh.body: Rarer cards weigh more: the largest Meme edition (3,941 copies, FirstGM’s, on the October 11, 2026 cycle) divided by the card’s edition. A 310-copy Meme is 12.71, a Gradient 39.02.
network.tdh.explainer.minute.boost.title: Boost.
network.tdh.explainer.minute.boost.body: Full sets, seasons and Gradients raise one multiplier on all you hold: 1.80 with a full set in October 2026.
network.tdh.explainer.minute.example: One copy of a 310-copy Meme, held 100 whole days by a collector who also holds one Gradient (+0.02 to the boost).
network.tdh.explainer.minute.diagramDesc: Three panels. Days: 100 whole days from the purchase to the snapshot, drawn as ten groups of ten days. Rate: two bars on one scale, the largest edition, 3,941 copies, and this card, 310 copies; 3,941 divided by 310 is 12.71. Boost: a scale from 1.00 to 2.04, the highest boost possible on the October 11, 2026 cycle, with one Gradient at 1.02. The card gives 1,296 TDH; with no Gradient it gives 1,271, and with a full set instead, boost 1.80, it gives 2,288.
network.tdh.explainer.minute.snapshot: TDH is computed once a day, at the last Ethereum block before 00:00 UTC.
network.tdh.explainer.minute.reference: FirstGM (Meme #8) is the reference card: one copy held one whole day adds exactly one base TDH.

network.tdh.explainer.verified.body: Two separately written programs, the Rust core and the Python reference, recompute TDH every day and are compared with 6529.io record by record. The latest day, from the public feed:
network.tdh.explainer.verified.point.pro: Three programs written separately from one rule, and the Rust core, ported from the Rust reference, reproduce all 89 conformance vectors in their latest builds (as of October 16, 2026).
network.tdh.explainer.verified.point.for: A Lean 4 model, still a proposal, proves that steps inside one transaction cannot change who holds which copies since when. A mint and its burn there can still change eligibility and others’ TDH.

network.tdh.explainer.faq.sale.title: Why can selling one card reduce TDH by more than that card’s score?
network.tdh.explainer.faq.sale.body: The sold copy stops contributing its holding days. If the sale also breaks a set or removes a Gradient boost, your multiplier falls on the rest of your holdings too. TDH is recalculated from what you hold; it is not a permanently banked balance.
network.tdh.explainer.faq.transfer.title: Do I keep my holding time when I move a card?
network.tdh.explainer.faq.transfer.body: Moves between wallets of your confirmed consolidation keep the original acquisition time. A move outside it starts a new holding period for the recipient. Delegation alone does not consolidate wallets. 6529.io accepts four consolidated wallets since October 15, 2026, while TDH-v1 groups at most three; which applies is pending an owner decision.
network.tdh.explainer.faq.new.title: When does a new purchase or newly minted card count?
network.tdh.explainer.faq.new.body: A copy needs a completed 24-hour holding period to contribute holding days. Newly minted Memes and Gradients also need to pass the snapshot’s separate 24-hour mint-age filter. An already eligible card can complete a set before its new owner has held it for a full day.
network.tdh.explainer.faq.set.title: Does a full set include the current season?
network.tdh.explainer.faq.set.body: Yes. You need every Meme card eligible for that snapshot, including eligible cards from the current season. When a new card becomes eligible, a full set you held may no longer be full. Individual season bonuses follow the eligible seasons listed above.
network.tdh.explainer.faq.rate.title: Why isn’t tomorrow’s change exactly my daily rate?
network.tdh.explainer.faq.rate.body: Daily rate is a guide calculated from copies held at least one whole day and the current boost. Whole-day boundaries, per-card rounding, transfers, newly eligible cards and changes in rates or boosts can all affect the next snapshot.
network.tdh.explainer.faq.xtdh.title: Where does xTDH fit?
network.tdh.explainer.faq.xtdh.body: xTDH is calculated separately. Receiving xTDH does not increase the base TDH explained here. Your TDH rate is an input to the xTDH system.
network.tdh.explainer.glossary.title: Glossary
network.tdh.explainer.glossary.intro: The words these pages use. These five are all you need to read your own TDH.
network.tdh.explainer.glossary.tdh.def: Total Days Held: whole days held, weighted by rarity and multiplied by the boost, summed over everything you hold.
network.tdh.explainer.glossary.cycle.def: One day’s calculation. Cycle N closes at 00:00 UTC of its date; N is the number of days since January 1, 1970.
The last Ethereum block before a cycle’s 00:00 UTC. Holdings are read as of this block, and ages are measured to its time.
network.tdh.explainer.glossary.edition.d: How many copies a card counts for its rate: the copies minted. Burns do not reduce it. FirstGM, and Memes with fewer than 300 minted, follow special rules (How it works, step 6).
network.tdh.explainer.glossary.rate.def: How much one copy-day of a card weighs, rounded to cents. A Meme’s is the largest Meme edition divided by its own edition; a Gradient’s, the largest edition divided by the number of Gradients, and at least 1.00; a NextGen token’s, the largest edition divided by the number of tokens in its collection. Older pages call it the HODL rate or edition weight.
network.tdh.explainer.glossary.base.def: A card’s whole days times its rate, rounded to a whole number, before the boost.
network.tdh.explainer.glossary.boost.def: One multiplier for everything a collector holds, from 1.00, raised by complete sets, seasons and Gradients.
One collector as TDH counts them: a single wallet, or up to three consolidated wallets under TDH-v1. 6529.io accepts four since October 15, 2026; whether TDH-v1 allows four is pending an owner decision. The two burn addresses also have identity records, but are never participants.
network.tdh.explainer.glossary.consolida: Wallets that confirm each other on the delegation contract, so they count as one identity.
network.tdh.explainer.glossary.sink.def: The registry’s sinks: the zero address and 0x…dead in tdh-v1.0. Copies sent there are burned; the sinks keep records but are never debited, never consolidated and never count as participants.
network.tdh.explainer.glossary.xtdh.def: A separate system that builds on TDH. Received xTDH does not change the TDH on these pages.
Boost schedules 1.1 to 1.4 are 6529.io’s versions of the boost, shown under Current boosts and Historic boosts. TDH-v1 is the exact written form of the current schedule, 1.4; tdh-v1.0 is its rule version.
network.tdh.explainer.glossary.validator: A program, being built, that computes TDH itself every day, signs the result and agrees on it with other validators.
network.tdh.explainer.glossary.rust.term: Rust core, Rust reference, program B, Python reference
network.tdh.explainer.glossary.rust.def: Separately written programs that compute TDH-v1: the Python reference, written with the specification; the Rust reference, written from it in a clean room; the Rust core, the Rust reference made into a library, which validators will run and 6529.io runs from the cutover; and program B, a second Rust program written from the specifications and the vectors without opening any other implementation’s code. Before signing, a validator checks the Rust core against program B; the Python reference is an optional third check (D125).

network.tdh.explainer.formula.label: The formula, for one card
network.tdh.explainer.formula.text: Days times rate times boost equals TDH, for each card, summed over everything you hold. For one copy of a 310-copy Meme held 100 days with one Gradient: 100 times 12.71 times 1.02 is 1,296.

network.tdh.explainer.minute.resultNote: The Gradient earns TDH of its own on top; your TDH is the sum over every card you hold.
network.tdh.explainer.glossary.raw.def: Whole days summed over every copy held, before any weighting: copies held 300 and 100 days give 400. The rate turns raw days into base TDH.
network.tdh.explainer.glossary.netting.d: Within one Ethereum transaction, each address’s movements of a token, the burn addresses’ included, are added up, and only the net change moves holdings (D131): a copy that leaves and returns in one transaction never left. Three things still read every logged step: the mint counts (editions, first mints), the underflow test and the log-position checks.
network.tdh.explainer.glossary.underflow: The check that no wallet ever sends a copy it does not hold. An input that fails it has no result.
network.tdh.explainer.glossary.finalized: An Ethereum block that can no longer be reverted. A day has a result only once the block after its snapshot block is finalized.
network.tdh.explainer.glossary.vector.de: A small test case with its exact expected values. A program conforms to TDH-v1 when it reproduces every one: 89 as of October 16, 2026.
network.tdh.explainer.glossary.root.def: A hash that commits to a day’s results. The cycle root binds the day, its snapshot block, the rule version with its registry hash, every wallet record outside the two sinks, each identity’s TDH per card, and the counts and total; validators will sign it. The wallet root is the tree of those wallet records, and the history root commits to every event read. Equal records give equal roots.
network.tdh.explainer.glossary.cutover.d: The day 6529.io switches from its current backend to the Rust core’s result, planned for about October 23, 2026 (D132).
network.tdh.explainer.glossary.classes.d: How the daily comparison sorts a difference: A, a deliberate difference from the old backend; B, an old-backend bug; C, the Rust core and the Python reference disagree; D, not yet explained.
network.tdh.explainer.glossary.items.def: D132 is one of the owner’s decisions; DEV-2 one of the specification’s deviations from the old backend; BUG-15 one of the old backend’s issues. Each links to its entry on the specification page.
The two separately written programs behind the planned proofs of each day’s result (D119). Program A runs the validators’ own code, the Rust core among it. Program B was written from the specifications and the vectors without opening any other implementation’s code; its TDH code is the validators’ built-in second check (D125).
network.tdh.explainer.glossary.memes.def: The three collections that count: The Memes, editions of many copies each; Gradients, 101 tokens of one copy each; and NextGen, whose tokens are weighed by the size of their own collection.
network.tdh.explainer.glossary.firstgm.d: Meme 8, the reference card: 6,529 minted, counted as 3,941 after a recorded burn. While its edition is the largest, one FirstGM copy held one whole day adds exactly one base TDH.
network.tdh.explainer.glossary.season.de: A run of consecutive Meme ids, from a start the specification lists. Completing a season raises the boost once a later season has begun; seasons 1 to 20 carry a bonus.
network.tdh.explainer.glossary.fullSet.d: At least one copy of every eligible Meme. Holding one pays the bonus of every boostable season at once: every season with a bonus except the current one. Each further full set adds a smaller extra bonus, which stops growing at 33 sets, at about +0.144.
network.tdh.explainer.glossary.stack.def: For one card in one wallet, the list of times its copies were acquired. A send removes the copies at the end of the list, normally the newest, and each copy’s whole days come from its time.
The list of every number and address the rule uses (contracts, sinks, season starts, bonuses), fixed for each rule version and identified by its hash. Programs read it and hard-code none of it.

network.tdh.explainer.verified.identitie: identity records equal: every collector’s, and the two burn addresses’
network.tdh.explainer.verified.how: The Rust core read the day from public Ethereum servers: the snapshot block’s headers were linked to a finalized block and the edition floors proven against its state, while the history before it is taken as reported. The Python reference, written separately, computed the day again from the Rust run’s input, so the two check the computation, not the reading. 6529.io’s backend computed the day from the transfers its own indexer collected; its files were fetched from Arweave and accepted only when its upload key’s signature and each file’s size and data root verified. Every compared field of every record matched.
network.tdh.explainer.verified.unchecked: The history before each snapshot is read from public log servers and taken as reported. It stays so, even once 6529’s own Ethereum node is synced, until the daily run checks the full history against that node.
network.tdh.explainer.found.title: Found by the checks, before launch
network.tdh.explainer.found.floors.body: The written edition-floor rule, meant for Memes below 300 copies, would have lowered 285 identities’ TDH by 111,494 in total on October 11. It was corrected the same day.
network.tdh.explainer.found.netting.body: A second, separately written program found that under the first netting rule, steps inside one transaction could change TDH. Every transaction is now netted alike.
network.tdh.explainer.found.lean.body: The Lean model showed that not every value depends only on a transaction’s net movements: a mint and its burn there still count. The rule now claims it only for who holds which copies since when.
network.tdh.explainer.found.difftest.bod: Five rounds of differential tests across four programs raised 22 findings. All but one, still open, are settled in the specification.

network.tdh.explainer.verified.private: The rule’s text (P26), its test vectors and the programs’ code are not public yet: P26 and the Python reference are in 6529’s private design repository, and the validator code is to be published when the owner decides (D116). These pages restate the rule. What anyone can check today: 6529.io’s signed files on Arweave, the snapshot block on any block explorer, and the SHA-256 the feed states for each day’s file.
